name: FL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Fine's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Fine at ~97% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+14 district lean, incumbent Randy Fine's roughly $4.3 million raised plus $3.7 million in outside support against Eric Yonce's $326,000, and Polymarket pricing Fine near 97% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no public polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin near R+16.
model.watch: Any late public polling showing Fine underperforming the district's lean, or a surge in Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign of a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Fine, the Republican incumbent, is favored to hold this heavily Republican Florida district against Democrat Eric Yonce, with a Libertarian and an independent also on the ballot. The seat's partisan lean of about R+14 gives Fine a strong structural advantage, and the favorable national environment for Republicans adds to it.

Money is lopsided: Fine has raised over $4.2 million and benefits from roughly $3.7 million in outside support, while Yonce has raised about $326,000 with little cash on hand and no outside backing. Prediction markets give Fine about a 97% chance of winning. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a double-digit Republican margin.
